thread:
ajay: Quick question — I'm going to flip a Service from ClusterIP -> NodePort to put it behind NLB passthrough. Wanted to confirm ExternalTrafficPolicy and healthcheck implications before I push the terraform change.

marta: +1 good flag to check. Are you switching because of TLS passthrough? NLB needs NodePort if we want the host port mapping, otherwise LB targets cluster nodes.

ajay: Yeah passthrough for client certs. Current plan: set externalTrafficPolicy: Local to preserve client source IP and avoid kube-proxy DNAT. But that means we need healthy pods on every node or targetGroup will mark unhealthy.

linda: Correct. With ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local the node only accepts traffic if it has ready endpoints. For NLB healthchecks we use a target type=ip (node IP) and healthcheck port=nodePort. If some nodes have no pods, they'll fail HC.

ajay: Ah — so options are: 1) keep ClusterIP + use NLB targetType=instance (route to node with kube-proxy) but then client IP is NATed; or 2) NodePort + ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local and ensure daemonset or wide pod distribution.

ryan: Another option is to run a small sidecar daemon as hostPort health proxy on every node so TG sees healthy nodes even if app isn't on that node. We used that pattern on payments service.

ajay: Good call. For the terraform diff I'm about to open I included the aws_lb_target_group: target_type = "ip" and port = var.node_port. Any other gotchas?

marta: Make sure you set preserve_client_ip: "true" in the aws-vpc CNI config/annotations? Actually for NLB passthrough it's preserved by default if ExternalTrafficPolicy=Local, but double-check CNI SNAT settings (SNAT for pods without hostNetwork can still happen).

linda: Also check service.spec.healthCheckNodePort is set when changing to NodePort with externalTrafficPolicy Local. Kubernetes will allocate healthCheckNodePort automatically, but for terraform-managed Service resource you might need to include it or accept dynamic allocation. If you pin it in TF, include the value in the TG health check.

ajay: Here's the service manifest I'm planning to apply (will replicate in TF):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: inference-gateway
  annotations:
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-type: "nlb"
    service.beta.kubernetes.io/aws-load-balancer-target-type: "ip"
spec:
  type: NodePort
  externalTrafficPolicy: Local
  ports:
    - name: https
      port: 443
      targetPort: 8080
      nodePort: 31043
  selector:
    app: inference-gateway
```

ryan: That looks fine. In TF make sure you don't also have a managed aws_lb_target_group that assumes instance targets. The TG must use target_type = "ip" and health_check { port = "31043" path = "/healthz" }.

ajay: Right. Here's the TF snippet I plan to add:
```hcl
resource "aws_lb_target_group" "gateway_nlb_tg" {
  name     = "gw-nlb-tg-${var.env}"
  port     = var.node_port
  protocol = "TCP"
  target_type = "ip"
  health_check {
    protocol = "TCP"
    port     = "31043"
  }
}
```

marta: One more thing — if you rely on k8s to allocate healthCheckNodePort and you recreate the Service, the nodePort value could change. For stable infra pin nodePort in k8s manifest and TF variable, otherwise coordinate rollout to avoid downtime.

ajay: Good call. I'll pin nodePort in both k8s and TF. Also will add the annotation to skip cross-zone load balancing? We want cross-zone enabled to spread.

linda: For NLB cross-zone, it's an account-level setting or LB attribute. If you need to set it per LB use aws_lb attributes in TF: load_balancer_additional_attributes = [{ key = "load_balancing.cross_zone.enabled", value = "true" }].

ajay: Thanks. Last Q: secrets wiring for TLS — we'll keep TLS termination at upstream (pods) so certs are mounted as k8s secrets. Any SRE objections to that vs. doing TLS on LB?

ryan: Sounds fine security-wise as long as certs are rotated and mounted read-only. For mutual TLS you probably need passthrough anyways so do termination in pod. Ops already has automation for SecretManager->k8s Secret sync if you want.

ajay: Perfect. I'll post a PR with the TF + k8s manifest, include a deploy plan, and tag @marta @linda for review.

infra-bot: Deployed plan preview available at https://ci.internal/plan/1234 — no resource delete, new aws_lb_target_group will be created. :white_check_mark:

marta: I'll review later today. Ping me if you need an emergency rollback plan.

ajay: Thanks all :thumbsup:
